definitions.explanation: Moral wrongdoing or the concept of evil, as opposed to good.

examples.english: The distinction between good and evil.

examples.japanese: {悪|あく}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{染|そ}まった→染まる：04254_somaru⟧⟦{人間|にんげん}→人間：03523_ningen⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{救|すく}う→救う：02063_sukuu⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{難|むずか}しい→難しい：00517_muzukashii⟧。
examples.english: It is difficult to save a person who has fallen into wickedness.

examples.japanese: ⟦この→この：00962_kono⟧⟦{物語|ものがたり}→物語：03634_monogatari⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧、{悪|あく}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{最後|さいご}→最後：01413_saigo⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{滅|ほろ}びて→滅びる：10881_horobiru⟧⟦{正義|せいぎ}→正義：05097_seigi⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{勝|か}つ→勝つ：01199_katsu⟧⟦という→という：09577_toiu⟧⟦{展開|てんかい}→展開：04542_tenkai⟧になっている。
examples.english: In this story, evil is destroyed in the end and justice prevails.

notes:
{悪|あく} refers to evil or wickedness as an abstract concept, the moral opposite of ⟦{善|ぜん}→善：00465_zen⟧ (good, virtue).

COMMON EXPRESSIONS:
- ⟦{善|ぜん}→善：00465_zen⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧{悪|あく}: good and evil
- {悪|あく}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{染|そ}まる→染まる：04254_somaru⟧: to be tainted by evil
- ⟦{必要|ひつよう}→必要：00846_hitsuyou⟧{悪|あく}: a necessary evil
- {悪|あく}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{道|みち}→道：00505_michi⟧: the path of evil
- ⟦{勧善懲悪|かんぜんちょうあく}→勧善懲悪：19740_kanzenchouaku⟧: rewarding good and punishing evil (a common story theme)

KANJI READINGS:
The kanji {悪|あく} has multiple readings with different meanings:
- {悪|あく} (noun): evil, wickedness
- ⟦{悪|わる}い→悪い：00908_warui⟧ (i-adjective): bad, poor
- {悪|わる}: bad person, villain (informal noun)

USAGE:
As a noun, {悪|あく} appears in philosophical, religious, and literary contexts. It is also common in fiction where themes of good versus evil are central.
